    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that when it comes to the holidays, it's best to expect the unexpected.
    • In a recent development, that mentioned, even the NFL is unpredictable, so it's up to us to try and see the forest through the trees and anticipate what could be on the horizon.
    • Recent findings suggest that it was a modest day at the office for the entire Bears offense in Week 11, but they edged out a 21-13 win over the Saints.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that when it comes to the holidays, it's best to expect the unexpected. Rarely do things go smoothly when everyone convenes for Thanksgiving, so it's the right idea to lie back and simply roll with the punches as they come in. For instance, you have no idea what that weird uncle will say at the dinner table, nor can you guarantee the turkey won't be overcooked. It's bound to go off the rails in some capacity, but the one constant that you can lean on is that there will be football to help distract you from the madness, including the dog running outside with one of the turkey legs.

    In a recent development, that mentioned, even the NFL is unpredictable, so it's up to us to try and see the forest through the trees and anticipate what could be on the horizon. Below, we're going to highlight a handful of storylines/individual performances from Week 12 that may surprise some people, but not us.

    All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.

    Recent findings suggest that it was a modest day at the office for the entire Bears offense in Week 11, but they edged out a 21-13 win over the Saints. For his part, Colston Loveland was targeted just three times. The tight end hauled in all three passes for 29 yards, but did have a thunderous touchdown in the second quarter. That score should serve as the appetizer for a possible eye-popping performance from the Bears star pass catcher in Chicago's upcoming Thanksgiving matchup with the Detroit Lions.

    According to recent reports, this is the first of two matchups between these NFC North rivals this season, and first place in the division is hanging in the balance during this holiday contest. The Bears are a slight road favorite, and if they want to prove the oddsmakers right, featuring Loveland would go a long way in that endeavor.

    It has been revealed that in Week 18 of last season (the last time Loveland played the Lions), the then rookie delivered arguably the best game of his career. He caught 10 of his 13 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown. Those receptions are still his career high. This season, the Lions have been extremely susceptible to tight ends, allowing the most receiving yards (740) and receiving touchdowns (11) to the position in the NFL. They're also giving up the third-most receptions (68) to the position group this season.

    This is a tasty matchup that Ben Johnson and firm should look to exploit to come out of Thanksgiving thankful for their ninth win of the season.

    Recent findings suggest that gambling angle to note: Colston Loveland's receiving yards prop for Week 12 is 54.5 (-109 to the Over). Loveland is +145 to score a touchdown.

    It has been revealed that the vibes surrounding the Rams have been off ever since they kicked off their season opener in Australia. A season marred by injury has seen this once-dubbed "superteam" enter its bye last week at 6-4, on the outside looking in on the playoff picture as the No. 9 seed. As they emerge from the break, however, there is an opportunity in front of them to climb back into the playoff picture, but they'll need a little help.

    In a recent development, first and foremost, they'll need to take care of business during the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game where they host the Packers. Green Bay is currently clinging to the No. 7 seed in the NFL at 6-4 on the season. A mere win over the Packers on Wednesday would temporarily vault L.A. into the No. 7 seed. However, if they want to hold onto it coming out of Week 12 entirely, they'll need to hold their nose and root for the San Francisco 49ers to defeat the Seattle Seahawks at home.

    That won't be a small feat as Seattle is coming off of its bye and the Niners are coming off an international game in Mexico City. That said, if San Francisco can fend off the defending champions, that'd create the necessary breathing room for the Rams to hold onto their spot in the playoff picture. If the Seahawks win, they'd draw even at 7-4 and retain the tiebreaker thanks to their superior divisional record. It's not an impossible needle to thread, but the Rams will need to get some help over the holiday weekend.

    Industry observers note that gambling angle to note: The Rams are -104 to make the playoffs. A Rams-49ers moneyline parlay pays out +159.

    According to recent reports, A QB controversy has been brewing in the Pacific Northwest, specifically between Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. That talk about a QB controversy has been almost exclusively external, however, as the Seahawks have noted that Darnold -- who has missed the previous two games with rib and quad injuries -- will resume his role as QB1 when healthy. Head coach Mike Macdonald also noted that the team is optimistic that Darnold's return under center will come this week as they emerge from their bye and take on the San Francisco 49ers.

    Darnold has been sidelined for essentially four games so far (injured himself on the opening drive of the season opener), so we've seen what the offense looks like with Drew Lock at the helm. He's led Seattle to four wins (3-0 as the starter), while completing 73.1% of his passes and a 125.6 passer rating. By the numbers, Lock has outplayed Darnold from what we've seen so far in 2026, thus bringing up the question of whether or not to keep Lock as the starter.

    Sources indicate that again, Darnold will be the guy whenever he's ready to return, so there is no real controversy yet. However, if/when he returns this week, he might be set up for failure, as the 49ers are playing as well as any team in the NFL right now.

    If Darnold struggles and the Seahawks lose to the Niners to drop them to 6-5, that chatter to slot in Lock as QB1 will likely reach a fever pitch, particularly with the division and wild card races starting to slip away from them.

    I flagged this in my Cover 32 column for Week 11, but it's worth highlighting yet again. The Pittsburgh Steelers are dangerously close to seeing their season fall out from under them. They were 6-2 entering Week 9, and upon their return to the field, have looked nothing like the club that appeared destined to make the playoffs amid Aaron Rodgers' final season. Pittsburgh has dropped two straight games over the past two weeks, which now has them starting to fall down the wild card standings.

    Sources indicate that at 6-4, they're clinging to the No. 7 seed in the conference, which makes Friday's matchup at home against the Denver Broncos as close to a must-win as you'll find in Week 12. The Broncos are a 3-point road favorite in this game, so the oddsmakers are projecting Pittsburgh to fall to 6-5. If they do, they run dangerously close to falling out of the playoff picture entirely.

    Temporarily, that'd happen if the Fresh England Patriots go to Los Angeles and beat the Los Angeles Chargers. New England would draw even at 6-5 with Pittsburgh but they own the head-to-head tiebreaker thanks to a Week 2 win. Of course, the Patriots will be without Drake Maye (fractured fibula), but things might be evened out on the QB front as Justin Herbert is currently in concussion protocol coming out of Week 11. That possibly sets up a Tommy DeVito vs. DJ Uiagalelei matchup that is a true coin flip.

    It has been revealed that while the Patriots could oust them from a playoff spot for this weekend, the bigger long-term concern is the Houston Texans. They are hosting the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and are 6.5-point favorites. The double whammy for Pittsburgh would be for them to lose on Friday, see the Patriots beat the Chargers to shoot them down to the No. 8 seed, and then the Texans beat the Ravens to push them to 5-6. That's set up a Week 13 matchup between Pittsburgh and Houston that could very well be the nail in the coffin for their season if they don't turn things around.

    Gambling angle to note: A Texans, Patriots, Broncos moneyline parlay is +329.

    It has been revealed that it hasn't been the sophomore surge that folks hoped to see from Judkins this season, as the Browns back has struggled to be consistent. His 3.4 yards per carry average is a tick lower than his 3.6 yards per carry over his rookie season and is averaging just 47 rushing yards per game (59.1 yards per game in 14 games as a rookie in 2025). However, Cleveland's "Sunday Night Football" matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders set Judkins up with a true bounce-back opportunity.

    The Raiders' run defense has been horrid so far in 2026. Coming into Week 12, Las Vegas is giving up the most rushing yards to running backs in the NFL this season (130.5 yards per game). Their 13 rushing touchdowns allowed are tied for the second-most in the league. The Raiders defense is coming off of a Week 11 loss to the Broncos, where rookie back Jonah Coleman steamrolled them for 111 yards on the ground and three rushing touchdowns.

    As he enjoyed his bye week, Judkins was probably licking his chops seeing Coleman post those numbers, knowing full well that he'll get to face them this coming week. Judkins, a 2025 second-round pick, has rushed for at least 100 yards just once in his young career. Well, it wouldn't shock us if he not only notched his second-career game with 100 yards on the ground, but surpassed his 110-yard rushing game from Week 5 last season for a new career-best mark. The Raiders have allowed a 100-yard rusher three times this season already.

    #96206. Tech Report: Predicting MLB's next mega contracts: Paul Skenes, Junior Caminero, James Wood and more in line to get paid

    Tech Report: Predicting MLB's next mega contracts: Paul Skenes, Junior Caminero, James Wood and more in line to get paid

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1236 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Baseball has a latest highest-paid pitcher.
    • This is the fourth straight offseason some sort of contract record was broken.
    • Industry observers note that next offseason's free agent class is not robust, and it seems unlikely any contract records will be set, but who knows, really?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Baseball has a latest highest-paid pitcher. Sunday evening, the New York Mets landed two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal on a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. Yoshinobu Yamamoto previously held the record for the largest guarantee given to a pitcher at $325 million. Agent Scott Boras came in well above that with Skubal.

    This is the fourth straight offseason some sort of contract record was broken. Last offseason, Kyle Tucker set the average annual value record at $60 million. The offseason before that, Juan Soto set the record guarantee at $765 million. The offseason before that, Shohei Ohtani set records every which way with his heavily deferred 10-year, $700 million contract.

    Industry observers note that next offseason's free agent class is not robust, and it seems unlikely any contract records will be set, but who knows, really? Add in the uncertainty created by the upcoming collective bargaining agreement and I don't think anyone can confidently say what the next few offseasons will look like, or when contract records will be set.

    Recent findings suggest that that won't stop us from speculating, however. Here now are 10 candidates to sign baseball's next mega contract, which we'll loosely define as a contract that makes us stop and say, "oh damn, that's a crazy deal." Sound good? Good. Let's get to it.

    It has been revealed that junior Caminero, Rays: Caminero and Hall of Famer Eddie Mathews are the only players in baseball history with two 40-homer seasons before their age-23 seasons. Power pays, always has and always will, and Caminero has power to spare. He is not scheduled to become a free agent until after 2030, when he'll still be only 28 years old. If he doesn't sign a contract extension that would no doubt set upcoming records for his service time level, Caminero will be in line for a Soto-esque deal come free agency, assuming of course he continues hitting home runs at this pace.

    Sources indicate that elly De La Cruz, Reds: De La Cruz reportedly rejected what would have been a franchise-record contract last offseason, beating Joey Votto's $225 million extension way back when. Still only 24, De La Cruz just turned in a sensational season, during which he went 30-30 and finished sixth among all players with 6.4 WAR. He is one of those guys who looks like he was put on this Earth for the sole purpose of playing baseball. De La Cruz is an all-around impact player, plus he's a high-energy player who plays with obvious joy. He is three years away from free agency and this is exactly the sort of skill set that gets a record contract.

    According to recent reports, paul Skenes, Pirates: You know you've set a high bar when a 4.2 WAR season is considered a disappointment and people spend the summer wondering what's wrong with you. The fact is, though, that Skenes did take a step back in 2026, and he'll have to return to his 2024-25 form to get a mega contract. Plus, he has to stay healthy, which is the unspoken "if" that exists with every pitcher. Skenes will turn only 25 in May and he's three years away from free agency. Even if 2026 proves to be his upcoming normal, he'll get a massive payday as a free agent. And if Skenes rediscovers his 2024-25 form, Skubal's record will almost certainly fall.

    Gunnar Henderson, Orioles: A year or two ago Henderson, 25, would have been in the favorites category. He took a step back in 2025, however, and then another step back in 2026. To be sure, a 3.6-WAR season is still very good, but this is becoming a thing with top young Orioles hitters, no? Adley Rutschman regressed from legitimate star to pretty good. Now, Henderson seems to be on the same track. Henderson is only two years away from free agency. If his 2027-28 look more like 2023-24 than 2025-26, then forget it; he'll get a mega contract as a free agent at age 27. Star shortstops reliably get paid handsomely.

    Recent findings suggest that jacob Misiorowski, Brewers and Cam Schlittler, Yankees: This year's Cy Young winners are both five years away from free agency, which puts them at a clear disadvantage in the mega contract race. If they set any records, it will likely be for their service time level with an extension. Otherwise, we're talking about staying healthy and holding this level of performance through 2031 before Misiorowski and Schlittler sign mega deals. The Brewers aggressively lock up their best young players. Based on that, Misiorowski is more likely than Schlittler to sign a record extension for a pitcher this far away from free agency.

    James Wood, Nationals: There are very few hitters I would take over Wood for the next five years. He is terrific, with easy power and a discerning eye, and sneaky stolen base ability as well. Wood's outfield defense is not good and might keep him from getting a record contract. Then again, poor defense didn't keep Soto from signing the richest contract ever, and Wood is about the same caliber of hitter. He just turned 24 and he's four years away from free agency. Offense pays more than defense and Wood is going to hit 50 home runs one of these years. If it happens before free agency, all the better for his mega contract pursuit.

    Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs: Why is the reigning National League MVP a long shot for a mega contract after a 10.6-WAR season? Because the Cubs wisely locked Crow-Armstrong up to a six-year, $115 million extension just before Opening Day. Furthermore, that contract doesn't begin until 2027. The Cubs have PCA locked up through 2032, his age-31 season. It will be difficult, then, for Crow-Armstrong to sign a record contract simply because free agents do not get paid as well when they're in their 30s. No one should reasonably expect 10-WAR seasons every year, but if PCA can continue at an All-Star pace through 2032, then maybe he'll get a record contract. It's not impossible. Just unlikely.

    Recent findings suggest that mason Miller, Padres: No, Miller will not approach Skubal's record, but he is already well-positioned to sign the richest reliever contract in baseball history. The current record is Edwin Díaz's five-year, $102 million deal with the Mets four years ago. As long as he stays healthy and remains this, Miller should break the reliever contract record, whatever it is, when the time comes. He is 28 and three years away from free agency.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that injuries have been one of the defining stories of the young 2026-27 NBA season, and while some teams like the Oklahoma City Thunder are unfortunately months away from relief, others are beginning to see a light at the end of the health tunnel. We're now nearly a month or so out from the early-season wave of losses, and on Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania gave updates on the health of several key absent players. Let's use that as a launching point to check in on a handful of injured stars.

    It took Indiana's star point guard a full season to recover from the torn Achilles tendon he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, but sadly, his return lasted just four games before he headed back to the sideline. Haliburton was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain in October, and according to ESPN, he will be sidelined for at least the next couple of weeks.

    For now, there is no firmer timeline than that, with Pacers coach Rick Carlisle saying in a recent radio interview that he didn't think it was "out of the question" that Haliburton would play in November, but he would not "put a hard date on anything.".

    Haliburton looked mostly like himself in the four games he played early this season, averaging just under 22 points and 10 assists. The Pacers have fallen to 5-10 and the Eastern Conference's No. 10 seed without him, and they are seemingly aware of the need for reinforcements. The Pacers "clearly are looking at doing something" on the trade market, with an upgrade on the wing viewed as a strong possibility, Jake Fischer said Friday on SiriusXM NBA Radio.

    In a recent development, A return to action seems further off for Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards, who had knee surgery in late October. Edwards spoke with reporters Thursday and said he has "no clue" when he'll be able to return to the floor and declined to offer a timetable, per ESPN.

    According to recent reports, edwards missed 21 games last year and dealt with a knee issue in the postseason. Despite a hot start, that included a 47-point outburst against the Cavaliers, Edwards continued to experience discomfort in the knee, prompting the team to choose the surgery route rather than have their superstar continue playing through pain.

    Sources indicate that "It needed to be done in order for me to be able to play without any pain for the next couple years," Edwards mentioned. "But who knows? Maybe in a couple years I might have to get something else. But hopefully not. I think I'll be pretty good.".

    Led by LaMelo Ball, the Wolves have excelled even in Edwards' absence. At 11-5, Minnesota sits at No. 5 in the Western Conference standings entering their game against the Grizzlies on Saturday.

    Leonard has played just twice this season due to knee swelling, but according to Charania, there is optimism that he will return within the next few weeks. Leonard has been dealing with patellar tendinopathy, more commonly known as "jumper's knee," TSN reported on Tuesday. That is the same glitch he dealt with throughout his 2019 championship season. SportsNet confirmed that reporting, while noting that swelling is not typically how that injury presents. SportsNet's reporting indicates that the swelling and jumper's knee are separate issues.

    It has been revealed that the good news on this front is that the reporting to this point indicates that the Raptors do not expect these problems to linger once Leonard returns. Toronto successfully managed Leonard's health through that title season, and is being cautious to start this year as well. However, his absence has certainly been felt as Toronto is in the midst of a six-game losing streak without him.

    Industry observers note that meanwhile, the player Leonard was traded for is just about ready to make his Clippers debut. Brandon Ingram is expected to return Monday against the Houston Rockets, according to Charania. Ingram suffered a partially torn Achilles tendon last season, which kept him out of the Clippers' lineup at the start of this year. His absence has been keenly felt in Los Angeles as the Clippers have scuttled to a 4-10 start without him. Los Angeles has both a bottom-eight offense and defense so far this season, so getting Ingram on the court should represent a helpful talent infusion.

    In a recent development, san Antonio's second-year star thankfully avoided a major injury when he fell on the court against the Clippers on Thursday. He will, however, miss 1-3 weeks with a left hip rotator strain. Harper was walking without a limp following the injury, per The San Antonio Express-News, a positive sign for his recovery.

    The Spurs have the NBA's best record at 13-3, but the story to watch as Harper rests is the performance of former All-Star De'Aaron Fox. Just beginning a four-year max contract, Fox has scored just 23 points in his last three games combined. He's averaging the fewest points and assists of his career since his rookie season. The Spurs had been starting their three high-profile guards -- Fox, Harper and Stephon Castle -- together early in the season. It was working, but with the caveat that that group never played a second without Victor Wembanyama. The Spurs are more than 40 points per 100 possessions better when their MVP candidate is on the floor.

    If Fox can't right the ship while Harper is out, that could open the door to San Antonio moving him to the bench upon Harper's return. The Spurs thrived last season with two ball-handlers, two shooters and Wembanyama in their starting lineup. The three guards are working because basically anything works with Wembanyama, but when the competition gets stiffer in the playoffs, it's going to be harder to get away with so little shooting in the starting lineup. That puts the onus on Fox to prove he still belongs in the starting lineup, and bouncing back while Harper is out will be a massive part of that.

    Tech Report: 6 lessons from Week 11: Kyle Shanahan is as good as it gets, plus a rookie RB earning a role

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that when I think about Thanksgiving, I think about going to my grandparents' house growing up.
    • According to recent reports, around midnight — sometimes later — we'd arrive at my grandparents' doorstep, weary but happy.
    • In a recent development, and then there was Thanksgiving Day, which meant football.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that when I think about Thanksgiving, I think about going to my grandparents' house growing up. We'd leave immediately after my dad got off work on Wednesday and drive from my hometown in rural Virginia to my mom's parents in Newly introduced Jersey. A quick stop at the McDonald's was the only time we'd leave our route. We'd drive extra miles to avoid traffic. I'd try, often unsuccessfully, to fight off sleep on the drive up.

    According to recent reports, around midnight — sometimes later — we'd arrive at my grandparents' doorstep, weary but happy. They'd always greet us with smiling faces, no matter the hour.

    In a recent development, and then there was Thanksgiving Day, which meant football. My grandpa, a die-hard Giants fan, would lead our collective yelling at the TV, hoping the Cowboys would lose, and we'd pity-root for the Lions, who seemingly never won.

    The results fade, but what I remember is my family being together. It wasn't perfect. It got harder as my grandparents got older. We'd laugh, we'd cheer, we'd wish it could last forever.

    It's been several years since then, but I still remember my grandparents waving us goodbye, my grandpa good-heartedly reminding my dad to go south, not north, on the turnpike. It felt like just minutes earlier, they had been standing in that doorway welcoming us in. It always went too fast.

    So ahead of our six lessons, let me give you a non-football one: Try to cherish this week. If you can do it with family, great. If you can do it with friends, great. If all you can do is call or text, great. It doesn't have to be perfect. Whether you watch every football game this week or none at all, I hope you're surrounded by people you love.

    Industry observers note that coach of the Year has become so misconstrued, and not just in the NFL. Every individual player award honors the best player, but for some reason Coach of the Year honors the coach whose team exceeds expectations most.

    So, once again, Kyle Shanahan's magnificent job will likely go unrewarded, simply because he's done too good a job for too long. An early congratulations to either John Harbaugh or Todd Monken for winning. They've done magnificent jobs.

    Industry observers note that but Kyle Shanahan is the best coach in the NFL this season. The 49ers just dismantled the Vikings to move to 9-1. They have won games in Australia and Mexico and Seattle and Dallas, all places with their own unique challenges. They have won games using wide receivers they never imagined having to count on.

    Thought you saw the best of Brock Purdy? Think again. I've written at length about why Purdy deserves MVP and is much more than just a product of the Shanahan system, but there's no doubt Shanahan has raised his game immensely. This offense is so well-constructed, so prepared for each and every task each and every week and so connected.

    Industry observers note that the Vikings love to blitz. Purdy shredded them with quick passes: 12-for-13 for 161 yards and two touchdowns on throws released in 2.5 seconds or faster. Minnesota entered the night leading the NFL in sack rate and pressure rate. It managed just one sack and a 29% pressure rate, both season lows.

    This is nothing new, by the way.

    Oh yeah, and Shanahan also made the excellent hire of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who has helped turn this defense from quite poor to elite.

    It has been revealed that it's silly that we'll look back and likely see someone else win Coach of the Year. Shanahan has never won the award, by the way, even though he's been the best or among the best in the profession for nearly a decade. Andy Reid, who's fourth all-time in wins, has won it once, back in 2002 with the Eagles. Sean McVay has won it once since becoming a head coach in 2017. Kevin Stefanski, a perfectly solid coach but nothing more, has won it twice.

    Again, even if he doesn't win "Coach of the Year," Shanahan is very much the defining coach of this year. He'd gladly take a Lombardi Trophy over any individual award, anyway.

    One day after Brian Flores' normally excellent defense was shredded, one of his disciplines had his best performance yet. Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones and his unit were terrific in a 22-20 upset win over the Bengals.

    Sources indicate that jones, like Flores, brings extra pressure, big time. Washington is third in blitz rate this year. Joe Burrow has destroyed blitzes all year, but on Monday night, not so much.

    According to recent reports, jones was without his best cornerback, Amik Robertson, but refused to back down. His corners played physically, aggressively and well. The safeties followed in kind. And while Cincinnati's running game has never been a strength, Washington turned it into a decided weakness. The Bengals' 14% rushing success rate was the worst by any team in any game this year.

    Jones has this defense moving in the right direction, too. In November, the Commanders rank 15th in defensive EPA per play; they were 23rd before that. They've done a good job stopping the run and limiting explosives, largely because they have the third-lowest missed tackle rate in the league. Washington hasn't allowed more than 23 points in a game since Week 5.

    There will be big-picture coaching questions in Washington if the team doesn't make the playoffs, but Jones has done solid work under the radar.

    It has been revealed that I wrote about this in our Week 11 overreactions, but the Steelers are once again a team with a winning record and little chance of winning a playoff game. Here, though, let's talk about the style.

    Aaron Rodgers is now completing 21.6% of his passes thrown 20+ yards downfield. While he is throwing way more of them this year — only Jordan Love has more than Rodgers' 51 attempts — they're mostly performative "See? I'll still take shots downfield" throws that are low-percentage floaters. Only Cam Ward and recently released Daniel Jones have a lower completion rate on these throws.

    The run game can be quite good. In fact, the Steelers are second in rushing EPA per play this year at 0.06. Earlier in the season, it seemed they finally had one truly sterling offensive aspect. This made them different.

    But when the run game isn't going well, as has been the case the last two weeks, Pittsburgh has nothing else. The Steelers are 4-0 when their EPA per rush is above their overall season mark and 2-4 when it is below it. Pittsburgh was at -0.19, second-worst of the season, in the Week 11 loss to the Eagles.

    The Steelers have been the same as they've been during this playoff win drought: poor quarterbacking, good-not-great defense.

    In a recent development, K. Pickett, M. Rudolph, M. Trubisky.

    Just a dull, stuck-going-nowhere team archetype and a franchise that seems fine with it.

    The Chiefs' three-game winning streak has coincided with a soft schedule. There's not a ton to take away from it in terms of Kansas City's standing in the championship-contending pecking order.

    It has been revealed that but on an individual level, Emmett Johnson is a beast. In his two starts with Kenneth Walker III out, Johnson has 134 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns.

    Emmett Johnson has now recorded back to back 100 yard rushing games since taking over for Kenneth Walker.23 CAR, 105 RUSH YDS, 1 TD, 4 REC, 38 REC YDS vs Cardinals.Johnson's OROY chances have skyrocketed over the last two weeks. https://t.co/dt5FdKVwLi pic.twitter.com/tNep8zsuxb.

    Sources indicate that johnson currently leads all running backs in 7.0 yards per touch (min. 50 touches). He also leads all running backs in tackle avoidance rate (36.8), which is also first and slightly higher than tackle-avoiding machine Walker III.

    Johnson has a true three-down skill set. Only 11.3% of his rushes go for 0 or negative yards, the fourth-lowest rate among all running backs with at least 50 touches, and he has turned several potential losses into gains.

    It has been revealed that walker is a stud. He'll be the feature back when he returns from his groin injury. But Johnson has proved he not only deserves a legit complementary role down the stretch and beyond, but with his pass-catching acumen, he can actually be a weapon, too.

    Industry observers note that the Colts got thumped 26-3 by the Texans on Thursday, and that somehow wasn't the worst aspect of their week. Not even close.

    One day after that, Indianapolis released Daniel Jones, and shortly after that, reports surfaced that at the trade deadline, the Colts had turned down the Ravens' offer of a fourth-and fifth-round pick for Jones (the fifth would be returned if Baltimore made the playoffs). Now, they get nothing for Jones and will carry a $35.2 million dead cap hit in 2027.

    If interim GM Ed Dodds wasn't already filling in for a fired GM (Chris Ballard), this would be a fireable offense. Maybe it is, anyway. The Colts sold away many of their franchise pillars but stopped at Daniel Jones?

    According to various reports, the Colts turned away multiple suitors for Jones, including Baltimore's potentially lucrative one; multiple suitors for Jonathan Taylor, who fetched offers for a second-round pick plus more; at least one offer that included a fourth-round pick for veteran defensive tackle Grover Stewart, who's 33 and in a contract year.

    Sources indicate that I gave the Colts a D+ in my trade deadline grades and, upon first reflection, thought I might have been a little harsh. Indianapolis did get decent draft capital back for the moves it did make. But now, I think that mark might be generous. Every meaningless hard hit Taylor takes, and every meaningless double-team Stewart takes on, is just that. Meaningless.

    According to recent reports, the Colts have very little young, cost-controlled talent. They don't have their first-round pick in 2027. They will have a latest GM and, likely, a new coach. They are arguably the worst team in the NFL in 2026. They will be in the running for worst team in the NFL in 2027 and potentially 2028. They just turned down draft capital for a player they didn't even want. If there were a class in mismanaging an enterprise worth billions of dollars, the Colts' front office could do a great job teaching it.

    If it feels like there's been a little bit of a midseason lull, it's because there has been. In November, there's been a ton of blowouts — seven games decided by 15+ every week from Week 8-10, and then a lot of byes and semi-competitive games in Week 11.

    But the league is cranking it up a notch this coming week.

    Recent findings suggest that the Bears have won five straight, but their last two are over the lowly Buccaneers and Saints, with a bye in between. The Lions have won six straight, but the last three are over the Dolphins, the Patriots (mostly without Drake Maye) and the Buccaneers. I'm a huge believer in "you can only beat who's on your schedule." But in terms of learning about these teams, the past few weeks haven't been very helpful.

    Recent findings suggest that that all changes this week. On Thanksgiving, the 8-2 Lions host the 8-2 Bears (on CBS and streaming on Paramount+, by the way!), which should be an absolute banger.

    Sources indicate that this is far from the only example. Get your nap in early, because later that night, Chiefs at Bills is a can't-miss. Buffalo has seemed almost bored — and certainly hasn't been very sharp — in wins over the Ravens, Carson Wentz-led Vikings, Jets and Dolphins. But they'll absolutely be locked in against their bitter rival. The Chiefs, meanwhile, have cruised past the Jets, Falcons and Saints after a tough loss to the Broncos. We have questions about Josh Allen's turnovers, Patrick Mahomes' deep-passing renaissance — is it real or fake? — and much more.

    The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets. It is far and away the richest pitching contract in history, crushing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers. The Mets still have other things to address, including adding another starter, but they landed the winter's best free agent.

    It should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the crucial offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Monday's hot stove happenings.

    Industry observers note that the Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Latest York Post. Suter will make $3.75 million in 2026, and there's a $3.5 million club option for 2027 with a $250,000 buyout. He is the fourth reliever the Yankees have signed this offseason, joining David Bednar (accepted qualifying offer), Tim Hill, and Jonathan Loáisiga.

    With the bullpen mostly assembled, the Yankees figure to pivot to offense the rest of the offseason. They need a third base upgrade over Ryan McMahon and a right-handed hitting catcher to pair with the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. It seems likely the Yankees will go with Anthony Volpe at second base and Spencer Jones in center field, but those positions can be improved as well.

    In a recent development, the Mets have agreed to a deal with free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, reports the Newly introduced York Post. It's a one-year deal worth $8 million, according to The Athletic. He will presumably pair with Jared Young in a first base platoon. We did not rank Goldschmidt, 39, among our top 50 free agents. He accepted a reduced role for the Yankees over the last two seasons and was a valuable clubhouse presence.

    It has been revealed that at this point in his career, Goldschmidt is no longer an everyday player, but he remains a solid platoon bat. He hit .317/.402/.572 against lefties over the last two years, compared to .235/.271/.337 against righties. Goldschmidt can still play a nifty first base as well. The Mets received the worst first base production in the sport in 2027. Even late-career Goldschmidt should be an upgrade.

    After missing out on Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays are now believed to be prioritizing Freddy Peralta, according to MLB Network. Toronto has a very good one-two punch in Dylan Cease and José Soriano. Behind them are Spencer Arrighetti, Cody Ponce (returning from a torn ACL), Trey Yesavage, and maybe Jake Bloss and Ricky Tiedemann. There's room for another starter, for sure.

    Peralta, Michael King, and Trevor Rogers are the best available free agent starters now that Skubal has signed. Rogers declined the qualifying offer and is attached to draft pick compensation, which perhaps makes King or Peralta more desirable. Any of the three would boost a Blue Jays rotation that has upside but not much in the way of reliability behind Cease and Soriano.

    The Dodgers are not expected to aggressively pursue pitching help after losing out on Tarik Skubal, reports The Athletic. They're comfortable letting things play out and seeing what shakes loose among second- and third-tier free agents. As much as the Dodgers would have liked to retain Skubal, they're in a spot where they didn't absolutely need him.

    Despite this year's biceps and knee injuries, Shohei Ohtani is expected to pitch next season. He'll join Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Blake Snell, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the rotation. Emmet Sheehan, Gavin Stone, and Justin Wrobleski are next in line, with prospects Jackson Ferris and Christian Zazueta not far away. The Dodgers could use another starter but aren't desperate for one.

    It has been revealed that the Mariners, Padres, and Phillies are among the teams interested in Red Sox outfielder Jarred Duran, according to MassLive. The Red Sox tendered Duran a contract at Friday's deadline and will now look to trade him. The Jake Bauers signing pushed Duran, who had a .266 on-base percentage in 2026, out of the regular lineup. A trade is the logical next step.

    Sources indicate that philadelphia and San Diego badly need outfield help and are obvious fits for Duran. Even if the Mariners manage to re-sign Randy Arozarena, they could use another outfielder, though Duran would be a less-than-stellar fit for a lineup that is already heavily left-handed. Regardless, it seems unlikely Duran will be with the Red Sox by the time Opening Day arrives.

    The Blue Jays, Phillies, and Yankees are considered the favorites for Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports MLB.com. The Cubs and Mets are believed to have interest as well. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers but is not regarded as a strong defender, and it is likely that he will play first base or a corner outfield spot in MLB.

    This past season, Sato, 28 in March, hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs and won Japan's Triple Crown. He is similar to Munetaka Murakami in that he has big left-handed power, swing-and-miss concerns, and defensive issues. Murakami is a much more patient hitter, however. Sato is an aggressive swinger and is unlikely to walk much or post a strong on-base percentage.

    The Blue Jays offered Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract in the $400 million range before he signed with the Mets, according to The Athletic. Meanwhile, the Dodgers never reached the point of making Skubal an offer, reports ESPN. Los Angeles was known to prefer a short-term, high-dollar contract to a long-term arrangement. Getting Skubal on such a deal always seemed unlikely.

    As for the Padres, they put forth an offer in the $400 million range but with deferrals that would have lowered the present day value, reports the New York Post. Skubal's contract with the Mets includes $30 million in deferred money, which will lower the present day value some, but not significantly. The exact deferrals in San Diego's offer are unknown.

    Sources indicate that the Royals and left-handed reliever Caleb Theilbar are in agreement on a one-year deal, per ESPN. Theilbar, 39, was excellent for the Cubs in 2025, but took a step back in 2026, pitching to a 4.86 ERA (87 ERA+) and 1.30 WHIP with 60 strikeouts in 50 innings pitched. He did strand 18 of the 23 runners he inherited, which is an adequate clip for a middle-relief type.

    The Royals recently acquired late-inning lefty José Ferrer in a trade and Daniel Lynch remains in the bullpen, so Thielbar could well be their third option as a lefty in relief.

    Industry News: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    Sources indicate that title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    “They are really good examples,” Arteta noted. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    According to recent reports, “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    Recent findings suggest that you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    Industry observers note that it can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    It has been revealed that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    City, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where fresh boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal indicated was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

    • Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Rogers as the No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the Chicago Cubs are signing free-agent left-handed starter Trevor Rogers to a five-year, $120 million contract, ESPN reports. He'll now frontline a Cubs rotation bereft of arms after Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson all left via free agency this winter. Justin Steele, Cade Horton and Ben Brown, meanwhile, are all working their way back from injuries.

    Rogers, who recently turned 29, is coming off a solid campaign for the Baltimore Orioles in 2026:.

    Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Rogers as the No. 3 overall free agent of the 2026-27 class and the second-ranked starting pitcher behind Tarik Skubal. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years. There are some lefty Zack Wheeler vibes here. When Wheeler became a free agent after 2019, he already had the analytical stamp of approval, and the belief was he could get to another level with fine-tuning and good health. That is exactly what happened. Lefty Wheeler would obviously be the best-case scenario outcome for Rogers, but the bottom line is he will play the entire 2027 season at age 29, and he throws strikes with four pitches that the pitch data models already consider above average. More than a few teams will undoubtedly see Rogers as a pitcher who is a tweak or two away from finding another gear.".

    Rogers took the next step in 2025, and in the 38 starts he's made since the start of that season, he's put up an ERA+ of 128, an FIP of 3.20, and a K/BB ratio of 3.82.

    The Orioles made a qualifying offer to Rogers after last season, which means they'll be entitled to a compensatory draft pick now that he's signed elsewhere.

    It has been revealed that behind an offense backed by unanimous National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong and an elite defense, the Cubs made it to the Wild Card Series before being swept by the Padres, but their pitching, both starting and bullpen, wasn't up to the task. Now, with effectively a blank slate, the Cubs are expected to be in the market for multiple starting pitchers, and Rogers is the first domino.

    Rogers' contract is now the third-highest handed out to a Cubs pitcher, behind just Jon Lester (six years and $155 million) and Yu Darvish (six years and $126 million).

    As James Harden passes Kobe Bryant on NBA's 50-point game list, Donovan Mitchell says he's underappreciated

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (521 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Harden is in the midst of his worst scoring season since his second year in Oklahoma City 16 years ago, but the 37-year-old turned back the clock some on Friday night with a 51-point performance in a Cavaliers win over the Pacers.
    • Harden's vintage scoring night saw him go 15-of-26 from the field and 14-of-14 from the free-throw line in typical Harden fashion for the 26th 50-point game of his career.
    • At 37 years old (and 86 days), Harden is the fourth-oldest player to score 50 points in an NBA game, passing LeBron James on that list and trailing only Bryant, Jordan and Jamal Crawford, who scored 50 at 39 years old.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Harden is in the midst of his worst scoring season since his second year in Oklahoma City 16 years ago, but the 37-year-old turned back the clock some on Friday night with a 51-point performance in a Cavaliers win over the Pacers.

    Harden's vintage scoring night saw him go 15-of-26 from the field and 14-of-14 from the free-throw line in typical Harden fashion for the 26th 50-point game of his career. That moves him into third all-time in NBA history for 50-point games, passing Kobe Bryant and sitting just five behind Michael Jordan.

    At 37 years old (and 86 days), Harden is the fourth-oldest player to score 50 points in an NBA game, passing LeBron James on that list and trailing only Bryant, Jordan and Jamal Crawford, who scored 50 at 39 years old.

    After the game, Cavaliers' coach Kenny Atkinson offered an eyebrow-raising comment calling Harden "top-10 all-time," which drew immediate pushback from NBA fans, but Harden is an unquestioned Hall of Famer and continues to put his name among the all-time greats on NBA scoring lists.

    His co-star in Cleveland, Donovan Mitchell, lamented that Harden doesn't get the appreciation he deserves at this stage of his career, and that he expects, much like Russell Westbrook, that it won't happen until he retires.

    "He won't until it's over with," Mitchell noted. "I hate it, but that's just the world we live in. We won't appreciate greatness. We didn't appreciate Russ in his latter years until now. It's like, 'Oh man, Russ was this and that.' It's like we forgot he averaged 28, 15 and 16 for a month. It's one of those things where we live in such a negative space. I hate it. At the end of the day, he doesn't care. And for me, seeing that, I don't care. It helps, but at the end of the day, that's just what the world is. It sucks that that's that way, but us in this locker room and guys in this league, we know who he is and we know what he's done for the game. That goes for not just him but a lot of people in this league. We don't appreciate what's in front of us on a consistent basis.".

    Harden has long been a divisive player among NBA fans. Some have appreciated his ruthless efficiency while others have hated the aesthetics of his mastery of the dark arts of drawing fouls. As Mitchell noted, few players have had as much influence over the game in the last decade-plus as Harden. From his massive stepback 3-pointer to his movement on drives to create contact, so much of Harden's game has made its way into the arsenal of most elite guard scorers.

    It has been revealed that fans will debate whether that's a good thing, but his influence is undeniable. As Mitchell noted, whenever Harden calls it a career, he will get more appreciation, but there will also be heated debates over his place in NBA history as one of the most divisive stars (from a play-style perspective, at least) of his generation.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Among sports fans, Carmelo Anthony is perhaps most synonymous with New York -- both upstate from his incredible year at Syracuse and in New York City, where he starred for the Knicks. But Anthony was raised in Baltimore and is extremely proud of his roots.

    In a recent development, so when Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made headlines this week when he said that the thing the city of Baltimore was best at creating was "criminals," Anthony felt compelled to respond. Humphrey was admonished by the Ravens, which sent him home for the week and will hold him out on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers. He also received scathing responses from Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott and many other prominent Baltimore figures.

    Sources indicate that anthony joined that group on Friday with an Instagram post that called on Humphrey to go beyond the apology he issued earlier in the week. Anthony wants Humphrey to join him, Scott, and others in the community to find ways to lead by example.

    I've been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn't a talking point to me. It's in my blood. I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take fro you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I've heard every joke and every headline my whole life.

    So when one of our own stands on our name and notes the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it'll get cut out, that doesn't get cut out for me. It doesn't get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn't get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner. And it doesn't get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment.

    In a recent development, marlon, I see the apology. I'll take it, man to man. But Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don't build anything. Presence does. I put my time, energy and resources in Baltimore because I want kids to have somebody who believe in them. That's the job when you wear this city on your chest. You don't get to rep Baltimore on Sundays and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday.

    So let me tell you what Baltimore makes. We make fighters. We make builders. We make people who were counted out from the day they were born and showed up anyway. We make teachers who buy supplies out of their own pockets, coaches who become fathers, artists the whole world copies, and returning citizens who turn their pain into purpose. We make Olympians, Hall of Famers, legends. We make ME. We make Tank Davis.

    The Mayor opened a door. Walk through it. And when you do, call me. I'll meet you there. Let's sit with these young boys together and let them hear from two men who wear this city that they are not what anybody says they are.

    According to recent reports, baltimore doesn't make criminals. Baltimore makes the ones who make it out. And the ones who come back. #B-MORE.

    The overwhelming response to Humphrey's comments in Baltimore has been to highlight the incredible work being done by leaders to improve conditions, decrease violence, and provide mentorship and guidance to young people in the city.

    Anthony echoed the mayor's invitation to join in that work in the community and offered to be there right alongside him.

    #96190. Industry News: Is Stephen Curry the real NBA MVP? It's hard not to think so when you watch the Warriors without him

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1560 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Is Stephen Curry the real NBA MVP? It's hard not to think so when you watch the Warriors without him

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, it's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books.
    • It has been revealed that after battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history.
    • Recent findings suggest that this current one is even worse.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, it's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books. So it's really saying something to start registering all-time marks of franchise ineptitude, which is precisely what the Warriors have done over the last week.

    It has been revealed that after battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history. The only other time this has happened to a Warriors team was in February of 1998, a few months after Latrell Sprewell choked P.J. Carlesimo. The total margin of that four-game losing streak was 104 points.

    Recent findings suggest that this current one is even worse. These Warriors have lost their last four by 109 points, and what makes it even more jarring is comparing them to the team that had won eight straight prior to Curry's injury. That 1997-98 team was trash all year, starting 1-14 and finishing with just 19 wins without ever winning more than three straight games.

    According to recent reports, these Warriors, on the other hand, were starting to look like a legitimate playoff-caliber team. A cynic would say that run of victories came against a softer schedule than what they have faced of late, but that qualification doesn't hold much, if any, water. That eight-game run included wins over the Denver Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Los Angeles Lakers, Miami Heat and an Orlando Magic team that has immediately gone on to win five of its last six.

    Perhaps the Warriors would have lost to the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs even with Curry. Hell, maybe they would've lost to the New Orleans Pelicans, Dallas Mavericks and Memphis Grizzlies, too. That feels unlikely, but who knows? Even with Curry, the Warriors aren't good enough to start checking off scheduled wins. But that's not the point.

    The point is how utterly incapable they have looked in losing these games. Not only have they lost each of these last four by at least 20 points, but they've also been held under 100 points in all of them. That's a combination of incompetence that stretches beyond a franchise mark. That hasn't happened to a single other team this century.

    Before we try to answer that, let's just agree upfront that Curry has little to no chance of actually winning what would be his third MVP. The Warriors almost certainly won't have a good enough record to put him in real contention. His across-the-board counting stats, even if he were to maintain his torrid early pace, are not going to match those of Luka Dončić or Victor Wembanyama.

    The only real chance would be if both of those guys, and likely a bunch of others, failed to meet the 65-game threshold, but the chances of Curry, who has already missed six games and isn't expected to be re-evaluated until around Thanksgiving, making it to 65 games himself already feel next to impossible. He may be past the maximum 17 games-missed mark before he even returns from this injury.

    Which is to say, what we're asking here is whether Curry, at 38 years old and in his 18th season, is still the most valuable player in the league (has he always been?), not whether he'll actually win the award, and the answer to that question, at least in its simplest form, could very well lie in his absence. Just look at this team without him.

    Eight-game win streak with Curry.

    Four-game losing streak without Curry.

    Admittedly, there's some cherry-picking in those numbers. Curry actually didn't play in one of the wins during that eight-game streak, and the Warriors still beat the Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 with a 122.8 offensive rating behind 37 points from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.

    We're also leaving out the aforementioned game against the Rockets on Nov. 11 in which Curry only played six minutes and the Warriors looked fine, or even good, in testing one of the best teams in the league to its limit. It also must be noted that Golden State lost its first three games of the season and looked every bit like the team many of us predicted would stink, all of which Curry played in.

    Recent findings suggest that still, the general rule applies. The Warriors go as Curry goes. That was true even in the golden years when the on/off splits, even with the likes of Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson still out there, always pointed to Curry as the clear MVP.

    "If I didn't have Steph, I would've been like every other NBA coach and lasted a few years [with the Warriors] and then gone and coached somewhere else," Steve Kerr has stated, openly admitting that Curry, and Curry alone, has been the difference between a journeyman coaching career and a Hall-of-Fame one.

    He's not lying. Have a look at the numbers.

    Recent findings suggest that even if you want to remove the 2019-20 season from the equation, when Durant had defected, Thompson missed the whole year and Curry only played in five games, Kerr is still a below-.500 coach at 74-96 without Curry in the lineup. This is a coach who has had all kinds of great players at his disposal over the years, and still it was always Curry in control of his and the organization's ultimate fate.

    According to recent reports, this is still the case for the Warriors, who continue to fall off a cliff without Curry. When he's been on the floor this year, they have registered a 59.6 eFG%, which would rank first in the league. When he's off, they fall to 49.1%, which would rank last.

    Even the defensive decline we see in Curry's on/off splits can largely be tied back to his offense. Without him, the Warriors are unable to create the same shots and, when their latest brand of shots miss far more often, they end up defending in transition on almost 3% more possessions. That's a big deal. It's meant almost five more points per game surrendered to fast breaks over this stretch.

    It has been revealed that the Warriors have produced an average offensive rating of 103.8 in games Curry hasn't played this year, which would rank as the second-worst mark in the league. All told, they are 26.3 points per 100 possessions better in Curry's minutes this season, per Cleaning The Glass. By comparison, the Lakers drop by 25.5 points per 100 when Dončić sits. Wembanyama is in his own galaxy with this stat, representing a 37.8-point decline in San Antonio when he's off the floor.

    Industry observers note that it's fair to say Wembanyama means as much to San Antonio's defense, where most of that decline happens, as Curry does to Golden State's offense, and certainly the Lakers falling off by as much as they do offensively, even with Austin Reaves as a legit secondary star, tells you everything you need to know about his impact. All of these guys are MVP players.

    According to recent reports, but only one, by subjective definition, can be the most valuable, and the simple truth is the Lakers and Spurs are outfitted with far more functional rosters independent of their respective superstars. In Golden State, there is just nowhere else to turn. Nobody to generate any kind of consistent offensive leverage. No gravity. No shot creation.

    After the Warriors took that 38-point beating against the Spurs without Curry, the rookie Lendeborg, who had, in total unfairness, been saddled with filling Curry's go-to-scorer shoes, said "it felt helpless out there," and that is exactly what it has looked like since the Curry variable was removed from Golden State's equation.

    To be fair, the absence of a player is an imperfect lens through which to view value for a bunch of contextual reasons, not the least of which is how a team like Golden State is designed to play -- a specific, Curry-centric ecosystem not particularly amenable to abrupt adjustments. These players are not as bad as they have looked without Curry over these last four games.

    Sources indicate that but by the same token, they aren't close to as good as they looked with Curry, either. I always laugh when my dad calls me saying things like, "This Pat Spencer guy can play!" Everyone looks like they can play next to Curry. And then he goes away and suddenly you're wondering how the hell this guy made the Washington Generals look like one of the best teams in the league. Is he some kind of miracle worker?

    Sources indicate that in a basketball sense, that's not far off. Curry's individual production is already virtually unmatched, but it's his exponential powers, his ability to compound the returns of those around him, that set him apart. It's early, yes. Perhaps the Warriors will figure things out the longer Curry is away. Probably not. But maybe they at least can return to competitive functionality. Until then, however, it's pretty hard to not think Curry is the most valuable player in the league when you watch the Warriors play without him.

    • Industry observers note that the New York Mets gave Tarik Skubal a record nine-year, $450 million contract Sunday evening and the case can be made that it was only the second-best contract they gave out this past weekend.
    • There was certainly no urgency on the part of the Mets to lock up Ewing, who would not have become a free agent until after the 2032 season.
    • Second, the collective bargaining agreement will expire at 11:59 p.m.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the New York Mets gave Tarik Skubal a record nine-year, $450 million contract Sunday evening and the case can be made that it was only the second-best contract they gave out this past weekend. On Saturday, the Mets locked up center fielder A.J. Ewing to an eight-year extension worth $95 million, with a club option for a ninth year. The 22-year-old Ewing is now signed through 2034.

    There was certainly no urgency on the part of the Mets to lock up Ewing, who would not have become a free agent until after the 2032 season. There might have been urgency on Ewing's part, however. First and foremost, he secured life-changing money after only five months in the big leagues. I will never ever begrudge a player for signing an early career extension.

    Second, the collective bargaining agreement will expire at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and MLB's various proposals have included not only a salary cap, but also contract limits. The league proposed a maximum five-year contract at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, and six years at 16% of the cap for players who stay with their team.

    Ewing's extension may not be possible under the next CBA. That's a pretty good reason to sign a deal now, and it may incentivize other young players to sign long-term extensions between now and the CBA's expiration next week. Here now are 10 players who could get an extension done under the wire this week.

    Recent findings suggest that the Brewers aggressively lock up their best young players, including signing Luis Lara and Cooper Pratt to long-term deals even before they made their MLB debuts this summer. Misiorowski, the reigning National League Cy Young winner, could qualify as a Super Two, meaning he would go through arbitration four times rather than the usual three. The Cy Young and All-Star Games will boost his arbitration salaries significantly. It might not be long before he gets priced out of Milwaukee. If nothing else, it would behoove the Brewers to touch base with Misiorowski's representatives and see whether they can find common ground this week.

    Because they can afford big arbitration salaries and avoid the inherent risk that comes with long-term contracts, the Yankees do not give out early career extensions often. Perhaps they'll make an exception for Schlittler, who won the American League Cy Young unanimously and now leads a rotation that includes three high-priced veterans (Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodón). Keep in mind that Schlittler was a seventh-round draft pick who received a $205,000 signing bonus. He's still waiting for his first big payday and might jump at a team-friendly extension to secure life-changing money.

    Although Munetaka Murakami got the attention, Vargas was the White Sox's best player in 2026. He offers a rare blend of power (33 home runs), patience (101 walks), and contact (126 strikeouts, a good total in this era). His third base defense has improved from poor to passable, which still isn't great, but is at least playable. There's no more talk about a permanent move to first base or even DH. Vargas just turned 27 and he's three years away from free agency. The White Sox are a team on the rise and making sure Vargas will be around beyond his team control years would be a tidy bit of business before the new CBA kicks in.

    Free agent after: 2031 for both.

    Recent findings suggest that benge and McLean finished second and fourth in NL Rookie of the Year voting, respectively, and like Ewing, they are the homegrown pieces who will supplement the well-paid veterans like Skubal and Juan Soto. I am certain the Mets and president of baseball operations David Stearns have at least broached long-term extensions with both Benge and McLean, and maybe something will get done with one or both between now and the CBA's expiration. My sense is the Mets would like Ewing's deal to be the first of several extensions with their foundational young players, not a one-off.

    In a recent development, the NL Rookie of the Year really fills up the box score and has the skill set that will balloon his arbitration salaries. Home runs, RBI, etc. That all pays very well in arbitration and the Reds may want to get out in front of it, and lock in Stewart at a discounted rate that nonetheless pays him well and gives him a nice payday. The Reds tried and failed to extend Elly De La Cruz last offseason, according to The Athletic. That ship may have already sailed. Stewart, though, might be more open to the idea.

    Free agent after: 2031 for Messick and 2032 for Bazzana.

    Sources indicate that it was under then-GM John Hart in the 1990s that Cleveland pioneered the practice of locking up young players to team-friendly extensions. Manny Ramirez, Jim Thome, and others signed deals when they were years away from free agency. They got paid and the team gained cost control over their arbitration years, plus a free agent year or two. Bazzana and Messick -- Gavin Williams as well -- are next in line for long-term contracts. Messick was the AL Rookie of the Year runner-up and the third-place finisher for the AL Cy Young. That will reward him come arbitration time. Bazzana, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 Draft, has yet to fully launch, but that's typically when the Guardians get down to business. They like to lock players up before they break out.

    In a recent development, under POBO Craig Breslow, the Red Sox have aggressively locked up their top young players, and it's been a mixed bag. There's been some good (Ceddanne Rafaela), some bad (Brayan Bello and Kristian Campbell), and some TBD (Roman Anthony). Tolle figures to be next in line for an extension. He's excellent and this year's third-place finish in the AL Rookie of the Year voting figures to be the first of many awards votes Tolle receives in the coming years. The Bello and Campbell deals going sour shouldn't dissuade the Red Sox from trying to extend Tolle between now and the CBA's expiration.

    Recent findings suggest that I think the Tigers and Dingler learned a little something about managing his workload in 2026. They rode him hard this year. Dingler started 80 of the team's first 92 games, came off the bench five other times, and frequently DHed when he wasn't behind the plate. Not coincidentally, Dingler went from an .831 OPS in the first half to a .631 OPS in the second half. The man's legs must have been jello. Anyway, Dingler looks the part of a franchise catcher both at the plate and behind it, and good young catchers are always worth keeping. The Tigers recently extended Troy Melton. My guess is they'll try to extend Dingler soon too.
