    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Ranking NBA's biggest winners and losers of the week: Knicks hit their stride, while Celtics take step back

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1685 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Let's call the last seven days the NBA's first parity week of the season.
    • The Western Conference is similarly crunched.
    • You're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the Fresh Orleans Pelicans, aren't you?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Let's call the last seven days the NBA's first parity week of the season. Take a look at the standings right now. The No. 2 through the No. 6 seeds in the Eastern Conference standings all have exactly six losses, and while the Philadelphia 76ers hold a three-game lead for the No. 1 seed, they've done so behind a preposterous 12-0 clutch record. When they regress to the mean, we seem destined for an Eastern Conference packed like sardines.

    The Western Conference is similarly crunched. The San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers sit atop the standings with identical 14-3 records... but seeds 3-9 are all separated by no more than two games. Even the Sacramento Kings got a win this week! The NBA has spent years tinkering in order to create parity, and right now, at least it's getting it. With that unofficial week of parity in the books, let's crown some winners and losers from the last seven days.

    You're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the Fresh Orleans Pelicans, aren't you? That'd be the easy starting point. We could just as easily kick things off with Luka Dončić's shooting dip, as he has quietly shot roughly 41-31-82 in his past five games, bringing his ridiculous offensive numbers down to slightly more mortal levels and making Wembanyama, for now, the slight MVP betting favorite. Totally reasonable. They're both contributors to his excellent week.

    Neither stands up to what Wembanyama did against the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. He shunked. That's a word that didn't exist when we woke up on Thursday. It is now, hilariously, a signature moment of Wembanyama's young career. He has apparently dunked so often, so violently that he suffered a hand injury that compelled him to try, and succeed, to shoot a jump shot at the rim.

    Did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    According to recent reports, the MVP race is for the season. The ridiculous numbers are for the history books. The shunk wins the week. Any time you suffer and overcome a dunking-related injury by inventing a new form of scoring, you win the week.

    It has been revealed that the champs have won five in a row and are 11-3 overall since their 0-3 start, but this isn't as simple as the Knicks suddenly looking like the Knicks again. Many of the early season problems are still persisting. Mikal Bridges hit the game-winner on Friday and still shot 3-of-12 on Sunday. Josh Hart missed all four of his 3-pointers on Sunday and is below 26% shooting from deep so far this season. The starters, as a group, are still getting outscored by almost 13 points per 100 possessions after struggling mightily in the past two regular seasons.

    Yet they just keep winning. There are obvious basketball reasons for that. Karl-Anthony Towns is getting every rebound, making every shot, and has readopted the playmaking hub role he thrived in throughout the postseason, particularly when it comes to assisting Jalen Brunson. The bench is thriving. Landry Shamet is shooting better than 45% on 3s and Deuce McBride isn't far behind. Tyler Kolek has a 61-to-9 assist-to-turnover ratio.

    According to recent reports, but there's something deeper here, a resilience and versatility that developed over last season's championship run that is sustaining thus far this season. OG Anunoby has missed the past two games. Towns missed the Blazers game. Bridges and Hart play most of some games and only parts of others because of their early season struggles. Yet Mike Brown just keeps pulling the right levers, and the Knicks just keep figuring it out. Championships can bring about this certainty. The Knicks aren't quite themselves yet, but they have an internalized confidence that came from dominating the playoff crucible a year ago that's paying off handsomely right now.

    It's hard to tell what we've seen from the Heat thus far this season that really deserves scrutiny. They started 0-4 in part because opponents weren't missing any 3s. They've gone 8-2 since, but they haven't beaten a single notable, fully healthy opponent during their active seven-game winning streak. No Evan Mobley against the Cleveland Cavaliers. No Jalen Duren against the Detroit Pistons. No Amen Thompson against the Houston Rockets. No... basically anyone against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday, though in fairness, Giannis Antetokounmpo missed that game himself. Miami is something of a Rorschach test so far. You're going to see what you're predisposed to seeing.

    But if we're going to panic during the shooting luck-induced losing streak, we're going to have to acknowledge the positives during the winning streak. The maligned Heat offense ranks in the top five over their past 10 games largely because Klay Thompson is shooting like Klay Thompson again and Giannis Antetokounmpo never stopped dunking like Giannis Antetokounmpo. Their core lineups featuring Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo are deterring rim attempts and giving up basically no corner 3s. Andrew Wiggins looks more like Andrew Wiggins since moving to the bench. As tempted as I was to give the third slot to the player development coaches for the Memphis Grizzlies after Cam Spencer's breakout 26-point game against Cleveland, the seven-game Miami winning streak gets the nod.

    Recent findings suggest that the Celtics were too clever by a half with their lineup decisions this weekend. They sat Jayson Tatum and Derrick White against the hapless Kings and then sat Paul George in the second half of that back-to-back against the Stephen Curry-less Golden State Warriors. They lost both very winnable games by a single point when they probably could have ensured a split and maybe even a sweep by aligning the rest. Throw in a 17-point blown lead to the Denver Nuggets and allowing a 40-point fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic and the previously 11-2 Celtics lost all four of their games this week. They're back with the Eastern Conference pack.

    It's too early to draw any real conclusions, just as it was too early to crown them Eastern Conference favorites when they were throttling the Sixers two weeks ago, but this week was a reminder of some of the cracks here. Their best player is coming off of a torn Achilles, and their second- and third-best players are in their 30s and have to be managed carefully throughout the season. You can get away with never getting to the basket as a team when you're an elite 3-point shooting outfit. The Celtics haven't been this season, and we're now in Year 2 of Derrick White's 3-point drought (and, for that matter, arguably Year 3 of Jayson Tatum's). Mitchell Robinson will put together a few good stretches and then regress back into the mess he's been for most of the season. Boston has been nearly 22 points stronger per 100 possessions with him off the floor this season.

    According to recent reports, the Celtics, given their playing style and roster makeup, are vulnerable to the ebbs and flows of an 82-game season. When everyone's available and they're making their shots, they're going to look unbeatable. This week is what happens when they're not, and considering how frequently that's been the case for them in the playoffs, it's something the Celtics are going to have to learn to play through if they hope to make it through this crowded East.

    Sources indicate that slowly but surely, the NBA's cellar dwellers are starting to come around. The Utah Jazz won twice this week. The Chicago Bulls have won three times since Caleb Wilson went down, and they pushed the Denver Nuggets to overtime on Sunday. The Kings got win No. 2 on Saturday, but also pushed the Los Angeles Lakers to the brink on Friday. There is still a whole lot of misery at the bottom of the standings, but all of these teams can find small pockets of optimism.

    Recent findings suggest that not the Bucks, who are now the NBA's last one-win team and owners of a 13-game losing streak. One of those losses came against Miami this week as their former franchise player, Antetokounmpo, throttled them for three quarters before they made the final score look respectable in the fourth quarter. They have the NBA's worst defense comfortably. Beyond a three-game stretch in which second-year guard Kasparas Jakučionis averaged 21 points per game, it's simply been a miserable season in Milwaukee, and it's one that could get worse any day now as the NBA investigates potential salary cap circumvention involving Gary Trent Jr. We all knew the Bucks would struggle with post-Giannis life, but this is worse than anyone could have imagined.

    Tyrese Haliburton has played four games this season at a roughly All-Star level. The Indiana Pacers are now 3-10 in all other contests, and ESPN reported Friday that Haliburton is set to miss at least another few weeks with a left hamstring strain. This is after a 19-win season played entirely without Haliburton a year ago. At this point, obvious as it sounds, it's simply become clear that the Pacers can't win consistently without their best player. That was obvious in a playoff context, but the regular-season implications here are starting to add up.

    Indiana is already six games out of a top-six Eastern Conference seed. Even when Haliburton gets back, he's probably not going to be perfectly healthy for the entire rest of the season just given his own history of durability concerns. The East's bottom four teams are thankfully so dreadful that there's probably a floor of No. 11 here, but Indiana will eventually have to pass someone -- presumably the Washington Wizards, perhaps someone else who gets bitten by the injury bug -- just to make it back into the Play-In Tournament picture. Even if they're there, their road to and through the playoffs becomes enormously precarious. It doesn't matter how dangerous you are in a playoff setting if you can't actually survive the regular season and make it there. It's too early to say that's where Indiana is headed, but the danger is very real.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After missing out on bigger name free agent starting pitchers like Tarik Skubal, Trevor Rogers, and Freddy Peralta, the Toronto Blue Jays have fortified their rotation by signing free agent right-hander Kaima Taira out of Japan. The deal is for $80 million over five years with an opt-out after the third year, the New York Post reports.

    Industry observers note that earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked the undersized Taira as the No. 19 free agent of the current 2026-27 class. Here's part of that write-up:.

    According to recent reports, "Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu confirmed on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.".

    For his NPB career, Taira has a 1.85 ERA with 676 strikeouts in 633 ⅔ innings in a mix of rotation and bullpen duty. While, as noted above, Taira may not profile as a starter in MLB, the Jays will likely give him every opportunity to stick in their rotation, given their need there behind ace Dylan Cease. In addition to the $80 million commitment to Taira, the Jays will owe his former team, the Seibu Lions, a posting fee per the MLB-NPB agreement.

    Recent findings suggest that toronto won the pennant in 2025 but backslid in 2026 to 83 losses and a last-place finish in the American League East. The offense was their leading liability last season, but the rotation also needed attention. That explains why they were very much in the bidding for Skubal and other premium starting pitchers on the market. It furthermore explains why they're willing to take a chance on Taira.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The NFL's 2026 playoff picture still has much to be sorted out over the next 11 weeks.
    • In the NFC, there are clear-cut teams that are out of the hunt: the Arizona Cardinals (3-8) and the NFC East cellar-dwelling Philadelphia Eagles (3-7).
    • Industry observers note that seven teams will represent the NFC in the postseason, with the final three spots going to wild cards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NFL's 2026 playoff picture still has much to be sorted out over the next 11 weeks.

    In the NFC, there are clear-cut teams that are out of the hunt: the Arizona Cardinals (3-8) and the NFC East cellar-dwelling Philadelphia Eagles (3-7). There's also a jam-packed upper level of the conference that could see its order of supremacy change like a shaken-up snow globe on any given week. The NFC West has the conference's top squad at the top of its standings in the San Francisco 49ers (9-1), with the 2025 season's NFC finalists -- the Los Angeles Rams and the Seattle Seahawks- lurking on the cusp of the playoff picture, with both having 6-4 records. All four teams in the NFC North — the Detroit Lions (8-2), the Chicago Bears (8-2), the Minnesota Vikings (7-3) and the Green Bay Packers 6-4)  — are all separated by two games from the top to bottom and would all earn playoff spots if the season ended today. The exciting part of this season is that several of the aforementioned playoff-caliber squads have plenty of remaining matchups against each other.

    Industry observers note that seven teams will represent the NFC in the postseason, with the final three spots going to wild cards. Which franchises will emerge from the crowd to grab their ticket to play playoff football into mid-January? Which hopefuls are too far gone to catch up 11 weeks into the year? Here is a ranking of the five teams still considered alive in the wild card chase, plus each team's projected end-of-season record.

    All odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.

    The Los Angeles Rams have won four games in a row to get back into the NFC wild-card hunt, but it will be an uphill climb to reach the postseason without their two best wide receivers. Puka Nacua, a 2025 first-team All-Pro after leading the NFL in catches (129), receiving yards per game (107.2), and receiving first downs (80), is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after knee surgery for an MCL injury. Davante Adams, who led the league with 14 receiving touchdowns in 2025, is still sidelined with a hamstring injury that could have him out for a few more weeks.

    That means quarterback Matthew Stafford, who has only been around league average this season with the No. 15 passer rating (92.8) and No. 13 expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.08), needs to find the higher gear he left behind in 2025. Plus, the Rams' two multi-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year winners, Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, need to stay healthy and perform near-peak to get back to the playoffs this season.

    Los Angeles successfully walking that tightrope to return to the playoffs will be rather difficult since they have the NFL's second-toughest schedule in the last seven games of the season. Their opponents have a combined .606 winning percentage, with games against the 49ers, the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2), the Seahawks twice, and the Packers. They'll also face the Cowboys (5-6) and Buccaneers (3-7) down the stretch.

    With their lack of passing-game firepower, it is hard to envision the Rams overcoming their end-of-season gauntlet to return to the playoffs.

    It has been revealed that the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks are starting to find their footing in 2026 with three wins in their last four games following a 3-3 start to the season. They also might have a quarterback controversy on their hands: Seattle is 3-4 when Sam Darnold starts, and they are 3-0 when Drew Lock starts in place of an injured Darnold this season. In their last game, a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10, Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards and 2 touchdowns while also losing two fumbles. His 158.0 passer rating was the second-highest in a game in Seahawks history, with a minimum of 10 passes thrown.

    Seattle is set to face the 9-1 San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, and coach Mike Macdonald maintains the team is sticking with Darnold (ribs, quad) if he is healthy.

    According to recent reports, "The plan is for Sam to start. Nothing official yet; we'll see how Wednesday goes, but that's the plan," Macdonald told reporters on Monday, via ESPN.

    It's been a rocky year for Darnold. He is completing just 60.2% of his throws (26th in the NFL) while averaging 211.1 passing yards per game (21st in the NFL) with 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions (29th in the NFL in touchdown-to-interception ratio). That hasn't been the case for 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. His 1,207 receiving yards lead the NFL and are the most through a player's first 10 games in NFL history. Smith-Njigba also leads the NFL with 10 receiving touchdowns, making him the first player in the Super Bowl era with 1,200-plus receiving yards and 10-plus receiving touchdowns in the first 10 games of a season. He is on pace for an NFL single-season record of 2,052 receiving yards.

    In a recent development, like JSN, Macdonald's defense is elite and can keep this team afloat. His unit is fourth in the league in scoring defense (17.5 points per game allowed).

    According to recent reports, unfortunately for the Seahawks, they have the NFL's fourth-toughest schedule over their final seven games, with matchups against the 49ers, Giants, the Rams twice, the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers, and the Cowboys. They also get to face the 3-7 Eagles. Seattle's defense can win games on its own, but they'll need Darnold to lock in to make a run at a repeat.

    The Chicago Bears are rolling and on a five-game winning streak. During the streak, the Bears have not trailed in 5 straight games for the first time since 1959, when they did so for six consecutive games, per CBS Sports Research.

    It has been revealed that chicago needed a game-changing impact performer along their defensive line, and All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has been just what the doctor ordered. He exploded for 3.0 sacks in the Bears' 21-13 Week 11 win over the Fresh Orleans Saints, bringing his total to 5.0 sacks and three consecutive wins in his three-game Bears career. Despite playing just three games with the Bears since coming over in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, he now co-leads his new team in sacks (5.0) with Austin Booker, who has played in all 10 games for Chicago this season. According to CBS Sports Research, Simmons is now the only player in NFL history with five-plus sacks and three wins in his first three games after switching teams midseason.

    In a recent development, the problem for Simmons, quarterback Caleb Williams and coach Ben Johnson is that they have the NFL's most difficult remaining schedule, as their opponents across their final seven games have a .657 combined winning percentage. Outside of a Week 14 matchup at the 1-9 Miami Dolphins, Chicago's other six games are all against teams who would be playoff participants if the season ended today. They have two games against the NFC North-leading Detroit Lions (8-2), a game against the AFC South-leading Jaguars, a game at the AFC's top-seeded Buffalo Bills (9-1), a game against the Packers and a road game at the Vikings in the regular season finale.

    The Green Bay Packers received great news on Monday: All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons is back and will make his 2026 season debut in Week 12, Wednesday, against the Los Angeles Rams. Parsons likely won't look like his All-Pro-caliber self on every play Wednesday night, but his presence lifts a Packers squad looking to stay in the inside of the postseason picture. At 6-4, Green Bay is last in the NFC North behind the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2) and the Minnesota Vikings (7-3), but they enter Week 12 as the conference's No. 7 seed.

    Sure, the Green Bay Packers' patchwork offensive line didn't give Jordan Love (220 yards passing, one touchdown, one interception on 17-of-27 passing) a shot against Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense in Week 10, when they fell 30-10 at Lambeau Field. He was sacked eight times, tied for the most in a single game this season with Deshaun Watson (twice) and Justin Herbert. Love made some strong throws when he had the time. Green Bay ranks dead last in the NFL in rushing offense (67 rushing yards per game) while leading the league in dropped passes with 25, six more than the next closest team. Love has also been hit 69 times this season, tied for the fourth-most in the league, even though he averages the NFL's fastest time to throw (2.68 seconds). Despite everything going against him, he leads the NFL in completions of 20-plus yards (43) while ranking third in passing yards (2,838), tied for eighth in passing touchdowns (20) and ninth in EPA per dropback (0.12).

    Industry observers note that love can carry the Packers' offense if given any time to throw. His defense will certainly level up with the addition of Parsons for the last seven games of the year. All of the NFC North teams have strong schedules since they have to play each other, but the Packers have a slightly lighter road schedule than the Bears, with the league's seventh-toughest schedule (.557 combined opponent winning percentage). Like the Bears, they have to face the Bills and the Lions, but they also have the one-win Dolphins, the Newly introduced Orleans Saints (3-7) and the Houston Texans (4-6). Four of the Packers' final five games will be played at Lambeau Field, and they already beat the Bears head-to-head this season as underdogs, despite backup quarterback Tyson Bagent starting that game.

    It has been revealed that despite the 35-10 thrashing against the top-seeded 49ers (9-1) on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 11, the Minnesota Vikings' Brian Flores-led defense is still the NFL's best. They lead the league in the following defensive metrics through 11 weeks:.

    Industry observers note that on the other side of the ball, Kirk Cousins steadies their offense in a way Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz could not. He helped lead them to a 30-10 victory at the Green Bay Packers in Week 10 by doing just enough (207 yards passing, 2 touchdowns, and an interception on 21 of 31 passes) while Flores' defense overwhelmed the Packers' battered offensive line. Minnesota is in both the NFC North title race and on track to be atop the NFC wild-card race going forward because Cousins is a Viking once again.

    Plus, their schedule lets up some down the stretch because they finished third in the division in 2025. They have the 16th-toughest remaining schedule, with opponents that have a combined winning percentage of .514. Outside of games against the Bears and the Lions, the Vikings should cruise the rest of the season. Their opponents include the Panthers, the 3-8 Fresh York Jets, the 3-7 Atlanta Falcons, the 5-5 New England Patriots without Drake Maye and the Commanders.

    #96167. Bengals may have been robbed twice by refs in final five seconds of stunning loss to Commanders

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (886 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Bengals may have been robbed twice by refs in final five seconds of stunning loss to Commanders

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Washington Commanders pulled off a stunner on Monday night with a 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals that wasn't decided until Drew Stevens hit a 26-yard field goal on a final play that probably shouldn't have been the final play.
    • Industry observers note that the officiating crew appeared to make at least two mistakes in the final five seconds, both of which went against the Bengals, and one of them involved the clock.
    • On the Commanders' game-winning kick, there were four seconds left when the ball was snapped, and there appeared to be two seconds left when the ball hit the net.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Washington Commanders pulled off a stunner on Monday night with a 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals that wasn't decided until Drew Stevens hit a 26-yard field goal on a final play that probably shouldn't have been the final play.

    Industry observers note that the officiating crew appeared to make at least two mistakes in the final five seconds, both of which went against the Bengals, and one of them involved the clock. When a kicker is attempting a field goal in the NFL, the clock is supposed to stop as soon as the ball hits the net (or the ground).

    On the Commanders' game-winning kick, there were four seconds left when the ball was snapped, and there appeared to be two seconds left when the ball hit the net.

    In a recent development, now, in fairness to the clock operator, the time left on the clock went down from two seconds to one second right when the ball hit the net, so stopping it with at least one second left is almost certainly what should have happened here. Instead, the clock operator let the time run out.

    It's pretty clear that there should have been at least one second left, but under NFL rules, the officials aren't allowed to add any time in a situation like this.

    ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk broke down the situation on the broadcast.

    Sources indicate that "The clock ran to zero, but there were still two seconds left when the ball hit the net," Yurk said. "So, by rule, there were two seconds left, but replay cannot restore time when there are two seconds or more if the next snap is anything other than a scrimmage snap. So because the next snap would have been a kickoff, they cannot, by rule, put time back on the clock. So it properly ended.".

    Yurk is essentially admitting that there should have been time left, but the NFL rulebook doesn't allow the ref to put that time back on in this specific situation.

    Sources indicate that "In a perfect world, the clock operator should stop the clock when the ball hits the net, and there would be two seconds left for a kickoff," Yurk mentioned. "But once it ran to zero, there's nothing replay can do to fix it.".

    If the Bengals had been given the extra second, they would have only had time for one play. That play would likely have been the ensuing kickoff, but if no time went off the clock on the kickoff, then Cincinnati's offense would have time for one last-ditch effort. At that point, the Bengals would have had a chance to throw a Hail Mary, which is an extremely low-percentage play, but anything can happen on a Hail Mary — just ask the Commanders about that.

    Sources indicate that A;FK;JD;KJF;LAKEJFLKJVAL;KEJL;JF;EFJ;LFAKJJAYDEN DANIELS HAIL MARY! @COMMANDERS WIN! pic.twitter.com/BsQ0Z84Rko.

    Not to mention, the Bengals have two of the best receivers in the league in Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, so a Hail Mary would have certainly added some intrigue to the end of the game.

    This situation isn't going to come up very often, but it seems like the NFL should have a rule in place to prevent something like this from happening in the future.

    One play before Stevens kicked his game-winning field goal, there was another questionable call, which the officiating crew also appeared to botch.

    With the Commanders trailing 20-19 in the final minute, Jayden Daniels made some huge plays to get them in field goal range. The biggest one came on a 42-yard pass to Antonio Williams that brought the Commanders down to the Bengals' 8-yard line. At that point, the Commanders didn't have any timeouts, so they hurried down the field so they could spike the ball to stop the clock.

    Washington ended up spiking the ball with five seconds left in the game, but the problem is that the Commanders' offense may have been lined up in an illegal formation.

    According to recent reports, in the NFL, you have to have seven guys on the line of scrimmage for each play, and you could certainly argue that's not the case for the Commanders here. The receiver at the top should have been on the line of scrimmage at the 8-yard line, but he appears to be about 1.5 yards off the line.

    Industry observers note that this isn't as clear-cut as the clock incident, but the Commanders probably should have been flagged here. That would NOT be a 10-second runoff, but it would have moved Washington's game-winning field-goal attempt back five yards.

    That might not seem like much, but Stevens' kick was veering left the whole way, and it almost certainly would have missed it if it had been attempted from 31 yards instead of 26.

    It was a windy night, and Stevens is a rookie kicker, so adding five yards to the attempt would have certainly been a big deal.

    According to recent reports, of course, both of these non-calls went against the Bengals, who will probably be making a complaint or two to the NFL this week. Despite the bad calls, the Commanders certainly did enough to earn the win, especially in the second half, when they scored on all five of their offensive possessions.

    2027 NBA Draft Substantial Board: Quentin Coleman's meteoric rise, Tyran Stokes stays at No. 1, returners boost stock

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open.
    • But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Big Board.
    • Inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open. There are still eight months to go before Adam Silver steps up to the podium to announce the first pick. Nothing has been decided yet. In fact, there's probably only about ten players total that can confidently say they expect to be a first-round pick at this point. Everything else is yet to be determined.

    But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Big Board.

    Inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects. They're still building their lists, sorting them into tiers, and will spend the coming months trying to establish their order.

    That's the biggest difference between those front offices and the public discourse about the draft. The fans want answers now, and the Twitter scouts are quick to make bold statements in hopes of saying they were right first. The experts who actually do this for a living recognize that the sole goal is to be right on draft night, and doing that requires them to not jump to any early conclusions.

    That's all critical context to understanding this big board update, which is, at best, a way too early look at the most relevant prospects. It should be interpreted in tiers. There are probably five or six prospects competing for the top of the draft, but that list could change. Maybe 11 who should feel good about their chances to be first-round picks. Everything beyond that is simply a battle that will continue to play out over the course of the next 8 months. Let's dive into the biggest storylines after three weeks of college basketball action.

    I got a first-hand look at Stokes last week at the Player's Era 8 in Las Vegas. He went down with a contusion midway through his first game, sat out the second, and returned to drop 22 points and 11 rebounds in the final. In totality, the signs of extreme growth that have characterized his early season play continued to be evident in Vegas. He was far and away the most talented player in high school basketball a year ago, but had developed a history of not living up to his potential, or at least not impacting winning to the degree that someone with his talent should. So, coming into his year at Kansas, the eyeballs were more about his maturity, reliability, and approach. Answering those questions has gone about as well as it possibly could so far. He's not only been engaged and impactful, but he's shown connectivity with Bill Self that makes him look coachable. He's also not gotten easily derailed by adversity, which is a reassuring data point.

    To be clear, for as good as he's been, there's still plenty of room for improvement. In high school, he had an instinctive way of improvising his way to the rim. In college, he's found that isn't quite as easy, even with someone like Tre Kaufman-Renn regularly clearing the way for him anytime he comes charging at the rim. So, while he's over-dribbling at times, his playmaking is real, he's asserted himself as a rebounder, his shooting is progressing, and he's starting to use his size in the post.

    The bottom line is this: most teams are looking for a potential alpha-type creator with the first pick. Stokes is your best bet in the 2027 cycle, by a relatively large margin at this point, but it's still too early to say he's a lock to go number one. I'd put that at about 70% at this point. Getting to the finish line will require him to continue trending in the right direction, making sure teams are comfortable with their due diligence in the pre-draft process, and also leaving open the possibility for someone else to emerge in the coming months.

    In a recent development, speaking of ascending prospects, no one has moved the needle more in the first three weeks of the season than Illinois' freshman Quentin Coleman. But for those who track draft prospects 365 days a year, the last three weeks are just a short spurt in what has been a rapid rise over the course of the last 15 months.

    In the 2025 EYBL season, Coleman averaged 11.8 points. 5.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists for a Brad Beal Elite team that won the Peach Jam Championship. To put it plainly, he was a role player, albeit a valuable one, on a team that was built around current Arkansas freshman JJ Andrews and utilized Trey Pearson, who is currently a freshman at High Point, as their primary ball-handler and distributor.

    As soon as Coleman's high school season began, though, we immediately saw signs of growth. Those signs continued throughout the course of the year, and he skyrocketed the rankings in the process. He also decommitted from Wake Forest and took a much bigger NIL payday from Illinois. While he finished with five-star status, it was immediately clear at the USA Basketball trials in May that even that was too low.

    Since arriving at Illinois, Coleman has continued the pattern of exceeding expectations. His skill level, feel for the game, defensive instincts, and nose for the ball are all as impressive as expected. The physical transition has been easier than expected. He's continued to develop more burst, physicality, and, as a result, playmaking.

    It has been revealed that at the moment, he's moved all the way up to No. 4 on the CBS's current 2027 NBA Draft Substantial Board, but we're not going to put a cap on what he could do given the unprecedented growth we've witnessed over the last 15 months.

    Industry observers note that there were a number of prospects who had a chance to be first-round picks in last year's draft, who opted to return to college basketball. While most, if not all, of them are probably making more money in college this year than they would have in the NBA, they are also making strides with their game, and in the process, helping their draft stock in what is widely viewed as a weaker draft than last year's.

    It has been revealed that we've been bullish on Amari Allen's chances of helping himself given his latest on-ball role at Alabama, and so far, he's done just that. The 16 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds per game on 52/50/82 shooting showcases both the versatility and shooting gains we were banking on. Most of all, though, it's his decision-making with the ball that has been glaring. His usage has gone way up, and his turnovers have gone way down. He has recorded 30 assists against just three turnovers through the first five games of the season. Add his hyper-competitiveness to the equation, and he's certainly helping himself.

    In a recent development, arizona significant man Motiejus Krivas looked like an NBA-ready defender last year. This year, it's been more of the same. He's massive, even by NBA standards, at 7-foot-2 and 260 pounds, but deceptively versatile and very smart with his angles. We're also seeing definite growth offensively, particularly with his skill set facing the basket. Last week's 18-point, 12-rebound, 4-block performance against UConn was one that captured all of his value, and a game that scouts will undoubtedly revisit.

    It has been revealed that meanwhile, his teammate, Ivan Kharchenkov, has gone from a defensive role player to Arizona's featured scorer, and is putting up nearly 23 points, 8 rebounds, and 5 assists per game. To put it plainly, he's been as good of a two-way player as there is in the country, and now looks like he could be trending towards the draft lottery.

    Florida's Thomas Haugh had a chance to be a mid-first-round pick last June, but the variable that gave many scouts pause was his shooting. This year, he's shooting it with much more confidence and rhythm, making 18 of his 34 attempts through his first five games. Simultaneously, he's continuing to do all the little things that made him so intriguing in the first place with his motor, physicality, rebounding, and defensive versatility.

    Speaking of shooting, Braylon Mullins is establishing himself as one of the nation's premier shooters, as expected, despite the fact that he's clearly not 100% healthy. Through his first five games, he's made 19 threes on 50 attempts, but it's been the types of shots that have really stood out. He's running all over the court, flying off screens, and making threes on the move, all while being the focal point of opposing defenses. In short, Mullins is making the type of tough shots that translate to the next level, despite not having his typical ability to separate.

    One of the defining characteristics of the national 2026 recruiting class was the number of prospects who had glaring potential, but had yet to put it all together. That list included the likes of Duke's Cameron Williams,  Ohio State's Anthony Thompson, Maryland's Baba Oladotun, Christian Collins,  Adonis Rayliff and Darius Ratliff, all at USC. Nevertheless, almost all of them commanded the type of recruitment and correlating financial commitment that suggested programs were willing to invest in their development.

    It has been revealed that so far In t those investments have not resulted in the types of gains we had hoped for. The Ratliffs, Adonis in particular, have showed some flashes, while Collins has only recently been cleared. Williams and Oladotun are barely in the rotation, and Thompson is playing, but not making the type of impact that anyone hoped.

    According to recent reports, now, despite the lack of immediate return at the college level, most NBA decision-makers are still playing the long game, so I wouldn't expect any of these guys to be given up on just yet. Nevertheless, their early struggles did have to be accounted for on the substantial board, which is why many of them are now outside the top 30.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
    • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
    • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their substantial-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    It has been revealed that sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

    Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

    It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the massive spenders.

    That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    According to recent reports, de Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    In a recent development, brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews mentioned: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    According to recent reports, “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

    Sean McVay on Puka Nacua: 'Can't say for certain' what his Rams future will be amid pending free agency

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1076 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is likely out for the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery for an MCL injury he sustained on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders.
    • "Yeah, we have a lot of guys that are free agents," McVay told reporters earlier this week.
    • According to recent reports, that makes it sound like Nacua will be back with the Rams, and there's not much to speculate about.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is likely out for the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery for an MCL injury he sustained on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders. Nacua is also set to be a free agent this coming offseason now that his rookie deal is set to expire, and Rams head coach Sean McVay delivered a mixed message about Nacua's future with the team.

    "Yeah, we have a lot of guys that are free agents," McVay told reporters earlier this week. "What I've tried to really do is focus on right here, right now. He's obviously a guy that is a very notable piece for us for now and for the future, but there are a lot of guys that fall under that category.".

    According to recent reports, that makes it sound like Nacua will be back with the Rams, and there's not much to speculate about. But a later quote indicated there may not be as much certainty on that front, mostly because McVay stated those words pretty much exactly.

    In a recent development, "I can't say for certain anything," McVay stated. "Here's what I'm not interested in: something being taken out of context because my focus and concentration are on a Friday practice, even though I know it's Monday. I am trying to see how well we can play as a team against an excellent opponent [the Green Bay Packers] on Wednesday night.

    It has been revealed that "When you go through the amount of free agents that we have, Puka is a huge part of the conversation that you love, but there are also guys that are part of his draft class. There are guys on our offensive line, there are some guys defensively — so there are a lot of guys that are up that, as of right now, would not be under contract. There are mechanics that we'd like to be able to try to figure out how to keep these really good players and people that we love, and certainly Puka is at the forefront of our mind.".

    According to recent reports, in addition to Nacua, the Rams have Kevin Dotson, Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila, Byron Young, Josh Wallace, Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Davante Adams, Omar Speights and Kobie Turner, among others, set to hit free agency this offseason. While the Rams' $75.2 million in projected cap space is the fifth-most in the league (according to Over the Cap), that's a lot of players. Many of the Rams' pending free agents are significant contributors. However, none of them is nearly as integral to the team's success as Nacua is.

    Recent findings suggest that nacua is the Rams' best offensive player. He is one of the best receivers in the league, and he's well on his way to being one of the best in recent memory if he can stay healthy. His 383 catches are the seventh-most all time through four seasons despite the fact that he's only played 3.5 years so far. His 4,906 receiving yards are the seventh-most as well. He's the all-time leader in receiving yards per game (96.2), and he's averged over 100 yards per game in each of the last two seasons.

    But he's also somewhat unreliable from a health perspective, as a regular visitor to the medical tent and someone who will have missed 17 of the team's 51 games over the last three seasons by the time this year is up. And he's had very public off-field challenges over the last year or so that resulted in a three-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The league reportedly did not know Nacua needed season-ending surgery when it suspended him and allowed him to serve the suspension during his stint on injured reserve.

    In a recent development, it wouldn't be surprising, then, if the Rams were at least somewhat hesitant to commit what it would take to secure a long-term contract. The best wide receivers in the league are making over $40 million per year. Jaxson Smith-Njigba averages $42.5 million per year on his extension. To lock Nacua in, it would likely take a deal that exceeds JSN's average annual value, given Nacua's track record.

    Meanwhile, the franchise tag is projected to be worth "only" $30.91 million next season, according to Over the Cap, so that may be an option for the Rams to explore instead. That would allow them to retain Nacua for at least next season, even if they don't reach a long-term agreement, while also letting them negotiate an extension and retain the ability to explore potential trade opportunities if they decide they don't want to commit to him long term. And it seems like him not being around long-term is at least a possibility in the ether.

    "Very uncertain, up in the air as it pertains to the future with the L.A. Rams because going into free agency he's got two different injuries, including a significant MCL injury that Sean McVay states will keep him out a few months," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler stated this weekend. "Probably ends his tenure with the Rams — plus the three-game suspension for the off-field stuff this offseason, so it's just not the kind of way you want to go into free agency with momentum. On the field, he's the best free agent in 2027 of any player, so the Rams have got to sort that out.".

    It has been revealed that fowler may have misspoken when he noted the injury probably ends Nacua's tenure with the Rams. Based on the rest of the quote, it seems like he meant that the injury will end Nacua's season with the Rams. But the idea that his future is uncertain at all is obviously notable, given how important he is to the team. If Nacua isn't going to be on the team, then the Rams don't have much to build their offense around in the future, whenever the post-Matthew Stafford era begins. They wouldn't exactly be setting Ty Simpson up for success if they decided to go that route.

    Because Nacua is so good and so vital to the Rams' offensive infrastructure, it seems likely they'll eventually come to an agreement on an extension. But the lack of certainty in that regard, both from McVay and in outside reporting, makes this situation one to watch.

    • Industry observers note that earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked Peralta as the No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that veteran right-handed starter Freddy Peralta has signed with the Baltimore Orioles on a five-year deal, the team announced on Tuesday. The contract is worth $125 million with no deferrals or options, The Athletic reports.

    Recent findings suggest that peralta, who will be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is coming off a campaign in which he didn't pitch up to his usual standards during a disastrous stint with the Upcoming York Mets. However, he did more like his old self following a deadline trade to the Tampa Bay Rays. On the Rays' watch, Peralta made a series of adjustments that helped him find better results on the mound, including being named the ALCS MVP.

    Industry observers note that earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked Peralta as the No. 7 free agent of the 2026-27 class. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "It has been a roller coaster year for Peralta, who flopped with the Mets, rebounded with the Rays, then faced the Brewers (his former team) in the World Series and lost. The post-deadline stint with Tampa salvaged Peralta's free agent year. They made several adjustments, most notably raising his arm angle and getting him to pitch exclusively from the stretch, and the result was a livelier fastball and also better command. He's still five-and-fly Freddy. Even the best version of Peralta won't pitch deep into games and can be a tough watch because he nibbles and throws so many pitches per inning. They tend to be good innings, though, and the guy never misses a start. Worst case, Peralta is a mid-rotation starter you can count on to take the ball every fifth day. The best case is someone who can front a contender's rotation. Fastball Freddy was always going to be a great bounceback candidate this offseason. The Rays just beat everyone to it at the trade deadline.".

    Peralta isn't far removed from a 2023-25 stretch for the Milwaukee Brewers that saw him top 30 starts and 200 strikeouts in three straight seasons. In 2025, he earned his second All-Star selection and finished fifth in the National League Cy Young vote.

    It has been revealed that "Freddy has proven to be a winning player who understands what it takes to compete and succeed on the biggest stage," said Orioles president of baseball operations Mike Elias said in a statement. "His professionalism, preparation, and commitment to winning will set a strong example for our organization and we believe he will have a significant impact on our team both on and off the field.".

    After losing Trevor Rogers to free agency (he agreed to a five-year contract with the Chicago Cubs earlier on Tuesday), the Orioles were searching for a new frontline starter to join a rotation that includes Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz and some combination of Brandon Young, Cade Povich and Trey Gibson. Elias has been hesitant to pay up for pitchers recently, but either his strategy has changed or he decided Peralta was worth the cost.

    In a recent development, the Orioles' disappointing fourth-place AL East finish in 2026 has raised questions about the state of Baltimore's rebuild, particularly amid stalled growth from its promising young position players, including Jackson Holliday, Gunnar Henderson and Colton Cowser. Would-be franchise backstop Adley Rutschman was traded to the Boston Red Sox at the trade deadline.

    Because Peralta was traded during the 2026 season and was thus ineligible for the qualifying offer, the Orioles will not be penalized a draft pick for signing him.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, we're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec.
    • Sources indicate that firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who prepares to do what in the months to come.
    • The 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers are headed for a titanic clash with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday that will presumably put one of those two teams in pole position in the Western Conference.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, we're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec. 15), we've seen enough basketball for teams to at least begin making plans for the upcoming transaction cycle. Teams are starting to know how good they are, what sort of holes they're dealing with and what the market is going to look like as we draw closer to the February trade deadline.

    Sources indicate that firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who prepares to do what in the months to come. So let's check in on what has made the rounds lately.

    The 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers are headed for a titanic clash with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday that will presumably put one of those two teams in pole position in the Western Conference. Last Friday, however, head of basketball operations Rob Pelinka did a pregame interview with Spectrum SportsNet in which he made it clear he aims to be aggressive ahead of February's deadline.

    "We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see," Pelinka noted. "We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get big-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great and we hope it continues.".

    The Lakers are very limited in terms of tradable draft capital because of their big July swing for Walker Kessler. They only have one first-round asset available, and it's only swap rights in 2032. They picked up two useful second-round picks in the Deandre Ayton trade, though, giving them three in total. That's not enough for a blockbuster, but it's helpful liquidity. Further, the Lakers are relatively financially flexible going into the deadline as well. They're barely over the luxury-tax line and have around $8 million in room beneath their first apron hard cap, allowing them to potentially make a somewhat unbalanced trade if the need presents itself.

    Sources indicate that so, what would the Lakers be looking for at the deadline? Two obvious needs stand out:.

    As Marc Stein noted, the Los Angeles Clippers have moved to a veteran-only starting lineup, with Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr., Max Strus and Brook Lopez opening games lately. Brandon Ingram, returning Monday, is sure to join that group, and Kris Dunn is a central part of their rotation. All of these players but Ingram and Garland are on expiring deals, and Stein noted that the Clippers are "regarded as a certain seller" ahead of the trade deadline.

    According to recent reports, and, well, that makes plenty of sense. The Clippers were just stripped of five first-round picks in the Kawhi Leonard scandal. Those expiring contracts belong to players who almost certainly won't be a part of the next great Clipper team, but they could help replenish the team's draft capital moving forward.

    The Clippers are, by far, the most versatile seller on the market right now. In theory, they could burnish just about any contender. Need defense? Jones and Dunn have you covered. Offense? Strus and Hachimura are proven playoff snipers. The center market is in the middle of a supply-demand crisis. Lopez has been sensational this season and could give any contender a solid 20 minutes per night. With Keaton Wagler in the building, it's hard to imagine they'd even shut the door on a good enough Garland offer. Expect the Clippers to live in the rumor mill for the next few months. They have several players who could legitimately impact the championship hunt.

    Industry observers note that last week, SNY dropped a stunner of a rumor: that the Utah Jazz, loaded with young guards and off to a terrible start, had had internal conversations about pursuing Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving. The rumor didn't make much sense in the moment, and The Salt Lake Tribune reported Monday that the Jazz "don't appear to have any real interest" in the future Hall of Famer.

    They have, however, talked trade with the team we just discussed: the Clippers. Those conversations began with "various Clippers bigs" and have moved on to wing depth, of which the Clippers have plenty. The Jazz are reportedly casting a wide net in pursuit of help.

    According to recent reports, the 3-15 Jazz have been among the NBA's biggest disappointments this season. A lot of that has been the result of injuries, with Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen out now and Jusuf Nurkić having not yet debuted this season. The Jazz are painfully thin in the front court at this point, and the early partnership between Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson in the backcourt has yielded mixed results.

    It has been revealed that casting a wide net makes sense since the Jazz could theoretically use help basically anywhere. More of a playmaking guard to balance out the score-first instincts that George and Peterson bring would make sense. Wing depth, especially defense-first wing depth, would help address a major weakness. Dunn is a former Jazz player. And of course, adding some size to deal with all of those injuries would probably have the biggest immediate impact. Utah doesn't control its own first-round pick this year. The Jazz benefit from losing in no way, and that has seemingly made them eager to try to fight an uphill battle back into the Western Conference Play-In race.

    #96156. Ranking NFL division races from first to worst: NFC North, NFC South entertaining for very different reasons

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (740 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Ranking NFL division races from first to worst: NFC North, NFC South entertaining for very different reasons

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the NFC East might be the best example of the NFL's unpredictable nature.
    • Sources indicate that then in Week 11, the division went 4-0 collectively, with the Eagles, Giants, and Commanders all springing upsets over AFC teams right now in the playoff field.
    • As Al Pacino, playing Michael Corleone in The Godfather Part III, remarked: "Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in!".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the NFC East might be the best example of the NFL's unpredictable nature. Earlier this season, it made history by becoming the first division to go winless over a two-week span in which every team played both weeks. Yes, that included the infamous Commanders-Giants tie that featured a fumble and an all-time clock mismanagement on the final two drives.

    Sources indicate that then in Week 11, the division went 4-0 collectively, with the Eagles, Giants, and Commanders all springing upsets over AFC teams right now in the playoff field. A $10 NFC East parlay of the Eagles beating the Steelers, the Giants beating the Jaguars, the Commanders beating the Bengals and the Cowboys beating the Titans would have netted you a handsome $345.51.

    As Al Pacino, playing Michael Corleone in The Godfather Part III, remarked: "Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in!".

    Ahead of a packed Thanksgiving week chock full of divisional matchups, we rank all eight division races, taking into account the quality of the teams involved, the quality of the races themselves and the potential for pandemonium.

    CBS Sports forecasting and projections:.

    The NFC North's main quest is potentially being the first team to place all four teams in the postseason. But the division race itself is a thriller, especially with Lions-Bears looming on Thanksgiving. Yes, Detroit looks like the clear NFC North favorite for now, but a Chicago win on Turkey Day would boost the Bears' chance to win the division to 45%. Regardless, this race projects to end in a thriller: In Week 18, the Lions play the Packers, and the Bears play the Vikings.

    CBS Sports forecasting and projections:.

    Industry observers note that does it get much better than a 50/50 split? Technically, our projections give Denver a 50.1% chance and Kansas City a 49.9% chance, if you're into that level of detail. The two teams have already played both of their head-to-head matchups (they split). The Broncos do have, on paper, an easier schedule remaining, which certainly helps.

    CBS Sports forecasting and projections:.

    All of a sudden, this division race doesn't look fun-bad and might just be ... fun! The Giants and Cowboys have the eighth- and ninth-hardest remaining schedules, while the Commanders don't face a team with a winning record until Week 16. A finishing stretch featuring Giants at Cowboys in Week 17 followed by Cowboys at Commanders and Eagles at Giants in Week 18 could provide plenty of twists and turns.

    CBS Sports forecasting and projections:.

    Recent findings suggest that last year, the Buccaneers beat the Panthers in Week 18 to stay alive, only to lose the NFC South on a tiebreaker the next day when the Falcons beat the Saints. Could we see similar madness this year? Week 12 will go a long way: If Tampa Bay beats Carolina on Monday Night Football, its chance to win the division jumps to 53%, per our calculations.

    The NFC South: It might be bad, but it's certainly not boring!

    CBS Sports forecasting and projections:.

    Even with the bunched standings at the top, our projections see Cincinnati as a clear favorite. The Bengals have several games where they should be huge favorites: Saints, at Panthers, at Colts, Ravens. It's far from wrapped up, though, and two games vs. the Browns loom large.

    CBS Sports forecasting and projections:.

    Recent findings suggest that the 49ers look like the best team in the NFL, and with a three-game lead in the division, this one might not have much drama. If that changes, it must start this week, when the Seahawks visit San Francisco. A Seattle win would only knock the 49ers' NFC West title chances to 81%, but it'd be a start.

    CBS Sports forecasting and projections:.

    In a recent development, never say never, but it's hard to see this one getting competitive, even after the Texans won and the Jaguars lost in Week 11. Houston needs another upset loss or two by Jacksonville. If that happens, remember Houston holds the head-to-head tiebreaker. That could turn up the heat.

    CBS Sports forecasting and projections:.

    In a recent development, with Drake Maye out until the final week or two at best, it would take something catastrophic (basically a Josh Allen injury) for this to be an actual race. And then, Tommy DeVito trying to chase down Kyle Allen would be more sad than fun.
